11 AI prompts every teacher should have in their back pocket
us.description: This article is republished with permission from Wonder Tools , a newsletter that helps you discover the most useful sites and apps. I’m excited to have a new semester underway. As a resource for my fellow educators, I’m updating a piece I wrote for The 74 , the nonprofit education news site. The average K-12 teacher works 49 hours a week . About a quarter of that time is uncompensated. In higher ed, adjuncts make up about 40% of the faculty workforce. At many institutions, time spent on course prep and administrative tasks is unpaid. Most teachers I know didn’t become educators to spend evenings generating quiz questions, rewriting instructions, or filling out administrative paperwork. AI assistants like Claude, ChatGPT and Gemini won’t change these realities. But when you’re overwhelmed, they can help streamline tedious tasks. They can free up energy for what only a human teacher can do. When used thoughtfully, these tools can actually push us to be more creative. They can help us overcome teaching ruts, nudging us to revitalize how we show up in the classroom. A 60-second guide to prompting The first step to making the most of artificial intelligence is understanding how to use prompts. A prompt is a natural-language instruction to an AI assistant. It doesn’t have to include technical or formal language. You don’t even have to use full sentences. Prompts work with any AI assistant. Use free private AI chatbots , like Proton’s Lumo or Duck AI . Or download AI apps that run on your laptop without touching the Internet, like Jan , which I tested and recommend. Claude, Gemini, and ChatGPT also work well. Whatever you have access to will work. As the teacher, you guide an AI assistant with relevant context. Prompts work best when they include specifics. Generic prompts yield generic responses. It helps to iterate on AI output with follow-up prompts. Ask for more specificity or detail. Adapt the response for your students. Don’t use it as is. Part of retaining your agency in the process is making sure you build on whatever outputs an assistant generates. You’re the director. It’s much like adopting an open educational resource . The advantage, though, is that this material will be more tailored to your students and teaching approach. Knowing how to use prompts effectively can mean the difference between AI that’s actually helpful and AI that’s gimmicky . The prompts below offer a creative boost. Each illustrates a practical way to use AI in support of thoughtful, pedagogically sound teaching. You don’t need any special technical skills. You don’t need paid AI subscriptions. Customize them to suit your subject matter and your approach to teaching. Start with a project If you want to use prompts more efficiently, first create a project in Claude or ChatGPT, or a Gemini Notebook . Think of this as a folder where you provide context about your class that an AI assistant can reference when you ask for support. You can upload past materials, syllabi, lesson plans, curriculum guidelines, Common Core State Standards, or whatever else is relevant for your teaching. You can also add detailed instructions to the project explaining how you’d like the AI to assist you. You’re teaching it your preferences. Once you set up a project, you won’t have to repeatedly type in the same context. The Prompt Collection 1. The Bell Ringer: Start class with a spark The first five minutes of class set the tone for everything that follows. A short, well-designed opening activity can draw students in. Engaging openers are especially valuable on Mondays, after vacations, or when you’re pivoting to a new topic. The challenge is coming up with fresh ones regularly. Goal : Generate five quick options for activities you can use at the start of a class session, adapted for your subject and your students. Prompt: “I teach [subject x] to students in [grade level x] . We’re studying [ specific topic xyz]. Generate five activities I can adapt to start a [xx] minute class. Each should take no more than [x] minutes, require no materials, and either activate prior knowledge or help students reflect on what they’ve just learned. Include one that’s discussion-based, one that’s written and one that’s a game or visual/creative task. [Or adapt these examples to reflect your subject matter. For example, one of the options could be a logic puzzle or an artistic challenge] .” Tip : Be as detailed as possible about your preferences. Include a sentence about your teaching style and context about your students. No need to make it formal. 2. The Real-World Hook: Answer ‘Why does this matter?’ before students even ask When you’re overwhelmed by administrative meetings, multiple preps, and paperwork, it can be hard to give extra attention to helping students relate to a new unit. This prompt helps you brainstorm connections to contemporary music, art, film, TV, cultural trends, or other subjects of interest to students. Goal: Generate five ways to show your students how the topic you’re teaching is relevant to their lives, each with a two-sentence hook you can use to open discussion. Prompt: “I’m about to begin a unit on [x topic] with [grade level x] students. [Provide a sentence of additional context and a few additional details about your students’ interests]. Generate five ways to connect this material to something students are likely to relate to. This can include sports, the arts, social media trends, pop culture, music, or other contemporary issues. For each connection, suggest a two-sentence hook I can adapt to help jump-start a class discussion.” 3. The Bad Example Generator: Turn common mistakes into learning opportunities Showing students examples of mistakes can help them avoid those pitfalls. But you can’t embarrass students by showing examples of their weakest work. Fortunately, AI assistants are excellent example generators. They can come up with nearly any kind of error you specify. No need to spend hours creating intentionally bad work. Adapt this prompt to include any kind of error you want your students to avoid. These can include experimental design mishaps in science or mangled math formulas. If you’re teaching essay writing, showcase logical fallacies or ad hominem arguments. Prompt: “I’m teaching [x subject/topic] to [grade level x] students. [Provide an additional sentence of specific context about your class, the learning goals you’re focusing on, and/or the lesson you’re preparing.] Generate five examples of paragraphs with [ad hominem arguments / circular reasoning / weak thesis statements / misleading use of statistics / or pick any other weakness] related to [x topic]. Make sure each example is realistic. These should be the kinds of errors students at this grade level might actually make. Don’t label what’s wrong. I’ll use these for a class activity where students identify and explain the flaws themselves.” Tip : You can also task the AI with annotating or explaining these errors to help you walk students methodically through these common flaws. 4. The Scaffolding Prompt: Make instructions clear for every student Complex instructions often trip up students. Simplifying language can help, along with breaking guidance into smaller steps. This prompt helps you clarify instructions for an existing assignment, handout, or any other activity. It’s particularly useful if you have students with learning differences or if your class has a wide range of readiness levels. Goal: Reframe a handout or assignment so it’s clearer and more accessible, especially for students who need extra support. Prompt: “Here is a [handout / assignment / resource] I give students: [paste or upload it] . Help me reframe this for students who face [specific challenges or context] . I particularly want this to be more accessible for students who need extra support. Break the instructions into smaller, numbered steps. Replace any abstract language with concrete directions. Point out any parts I should clarify. Suggest a brief example for each major step and any illustrations or images that might help me make this more visually engaging. Maintain the academic expectations I have for the work.” 5. The Review Game Generator: Develop review questions efficiently Coming up with a long list of review questions can take hours. And designing plausible wrong answers can be exhausting. An AI assistant can help, quickly turning existing handouts, lesson plans, or fact sheets into engaging questions, customized for your subject and student level. Tip: Add questions you’ve used in the past to the prompt as a model for the AI assistant to learn from. Goal: Generate 15 multiple-choice review questions, tiered by difficulty, formatted for whatever learning game you prefer. Prompt: “I’m finishing a unit on [x topic] with my [grade level x] students. For an upcoming review session, I’m preparing material to help students practice [a particular skill or area of knowledge] . Generate 15 questions based on the following key concepts: [list concepts or paste notes or upload a handout] . For the multiple-choice ones, include a correct answer and three plausible wrong answers. Vary the difficulty: five easy, five medium, five challenging. Flag the correct answer for each. Also suggest some true/false, fill-in-the-blank, and open-ended questions for variety.” 6. The Fresh Angle Search: Bring new life to familiar content Some topics get stale, especially when you’ve taught them the same way for years. To liven up an old lesson, it can be helpful to gather new sources, examples, statistics, case studies, or unexpected angles. Use Perplexity , a free, AI-powered search engine that provides citations alongside its results. Its links ensure you have an evidence trail to verify its responses and explore the original sources. Digging into Perplexity’s concise search summary is more efficient than sorting through hundreds of Google links. Goal : Find five recent or unexpected real-world examples of a concept you’re teaching, including perspectives from outside the U.S. and connections to students’ current interests. Prompt: “I teach [x topic] to [grade level x] students. [Provide additional context here about the topic or learning outcomes you’re focused on] . I’m looking for interesting material [or whatever other description you prefer] to make this subject more engaging for students. [Include any additional context about your students’ interests] . Find me several recent, unexpected or counterintuitive real-world examples of [x concept] that might surprise or intrigue students. Include real-world details to help add nuance for students who think they already understand the concept. And suggest multiple new analogies I can use for students who don’t yet understand this concept. Include international examples, and at least one that has an element of humor.” 7. The Skeptical Student Prompt: Prepare for the hardest questions before class starts You never know what odd questions might arise when you teach a new topic. AI assistants can help by generating all sorts of potential questions. That prep can help you avoid unpleasant surprises in class, so you’re ready for nearly anything students might toss at you. Goal: Generate 10 challenging questions a skeptical student might ask me about this lesson. Prompt: “Here is a [lesson plan / reading / concept ] I’m teaching: [ paste or upload material, mentioning the grade level and any other relevant context] . Give me a list of potential student questions about the relevance of this new topic and about real-world applications. Also note any doubts students might have. If these students [ at grade level x ] are skeptical that this material is relevant, what might they wonder, and what aspects in particular might they question? Generate 10 challenging questions curious students might ask. Include ones that challenge the relevance of the topic, the reliability of my sources, and the assumptions behind my explanations.” 8. The Blind Spot Audit: Find your own blind spots before students do During a typical week, we don’t always have time to trade peer feedback on lesson plans or syllabi. But we can still benefit from getting input on our materials. AI assistants can critically evaluate your materials for clarity, accessibility, inclusivity, or blind spots. You always have the option of ignoring the observations. I usually like at least a couple of the proposed adjustments. Goal: Identify specific places in my lesson plan or syllabus where I might have an unconscious bias, where my instructions may be unclear, or where my examples may not reflect the diversity of my students. Point out any unnecessary jargon and highlight assessment criteria that might be confusing. Prompt: “Here is my [lesson plan / syllabus / unit overview] : [paste or upload document] . Take the perspective of a critic with expertise in inclusive pedagogy and student-centered design. Identify parts of my plan that may not work for students with vision, hearing, or mobility impairments. Also point out places where an unconscious bias might be influencing the way I’m presenting this topic. Point out places where examples or explanations I’ve included might not make sense to my diverse students. Show me places where my assessment criteria could be clearer. Note any other sections of the material that might not be inclusive, accessible or relatable for students. Be direct. Include the location of each issue so I can explore potential fixes. I want specific critique, not general praise. Explain each observation in detail.” 9. The Differentiation Prompt: Adapt an assignment for distinct levels In many classrooms, students arrive at varying levels of readiness. But consistently creating multiple versions of the same material can turn 40-hour weeks into 49-hour marathons. An AI assistant’s suggested adaptations can help. Tip : Make sure your differentiated materials remain anchored in your own ideas and teaching goals. There’s a risk of cognitive offloading, where you start letting the AI make decisions for you. Avoid that by treating any response you get as a preliminary thought that you shape yourself. Goal: Produce alternative versions of an existing assignment: one with additional scaffolding, and one with stretch challenges for advanced students. Prompt: “Here is an [assignment / assessment] I give students: [paste or upload material] . Generate two versions of this: one for students who need additional scaffolding and more explicit guidance, and one that adds stretch challenges for advanced students. Preserve the core learning objectives. Summarize the suggested changes and explain their rationale, so I can decide how to adapt these alternatives for my students.” 10. The Rubric Builder: Help students understand how you’ll assess them A well-designed rubric does two things: It clarifies your expectations before students start working, and it gives them a road map for revising. Developing rubrics from scratch is tedious. It requires formatting small batches of text into boxes in complex tables. This prompt generates a structured first draft in table format. You can then refine it before sharing it with students. To start, specify the elements of the student work you’ll be evaluating, and describe your criteria. You don’t have to use full sentences or formal language. Just describe what constitutes excellence for this assignment, what satisfactory work looks like, and what evidence signals to you that a student may need more practice. Crafting these rubrics with AI assistance is an iterative process. Revise initial outputs by adding your own details and refinements. Goal: Generate a rubric written in clear, concrete language that helps students understand how they’re going to be evaluated. Prompt: “I’m assigning [assignment description] to [grade level x] students. [Here’s a bit of relevant context] . Generate a rubric with three performance levels: Excellent, Proficient, and Developing. (Or Superb, Good, and Needs Improvement.) Include five criteria relevant to this assignment: [list criteria, e.g., use of evidence, originality, thoughtfulness, structure, and mechanics] . For each criterion and each level, write two specific sentences describing what that performance actually looks like. Avoid vague language like ‘good use of sources.’ Put this rubric into a table, then wait for my edits.” 11. The Case Study Collaborator: Generate fictional scenarios to spice up discussions Case studies help spark lively discussions. They’re useful whether you’re introducing students to ethical questions or trying to help students relate to a historical situation. They can also bring a business decision or scientific discovery to life. Creating cases from scratch can be grueling. So this prompt helps you build fictional but realistic scenarios customized to your subject matter and student context. Goal: Create a fictional case study to illustrate a tension relevant to your subject, set in a context students can relate to, ending with three discussion questions. Prompt: “I teach [x subject] to [grade level x] students. [Provide an additional sentence of context or specifics to ensure the case studies are relevant and useful.] We’re exploring [x concept or issue. Include as much detail as possible about what and how you’re approaching the topic and your learning goals] . Create a fictional but realistic case study I can use in class next week that is timely and involves [a relevant character, institution, or situation] that illustrates the tension between [value A] and [value B] . Set it in [context relevant to your students: a school, a local community, a specific industry] . Make sure the scenario is complex enough that reasonable people could disagree about what response makes the most sense. End with three discussion questions that I can adapt to push students to apply the concepts we’ve been studying.” A final thought AI assistants have arrived at a time when teachers need support to do their best work. In a national survey by the RAND Corporation, just 24% of teachers reported being satisfied with their total weekly hours worked, and 66% said their base salary was inadequate. AI tools won’t make up for unfair compensation. But they can help us strengthen how we serve our students while we make time for the rest of our lives. gb.title: India snub Naqvi again as trophy row overshadows Asia Cup triumph
gb.description: India's women refused to collect the Asia Cup trophy from PCB chief Mohsin Naqvi Move repeats the men's team's snub of Naqvi last year, whose trophy remains uncollected Presentation delayed nearly 50 minutes before ending abruptly, with India handing their own players medals Coach Amol Muzumdar backed BCCI's stance: "We are the champions, that's good enough" INDIA's women's cricket team refused to collect the Asia Cup trophy from Pakistan Cricket Board chief Mohsin Naqvi on Sunday, leaving the presentation ceremony to end in disarray despite the team winning a record-extending eighth continental title. India hammered Sri Lanka by 72 runs in the T20 final in Dubai, but Harmanpreet Kaur's side skipped the trophy presentation altogether, repeating the stance taken by India's men's team last year. On both occasions, the trophy was supposed to have been handed over by Naqvi in his role as head of the Asian Cricket Council. Naqvi is also Pakistan's interior minister and head of the country's cricket board — a combination of roles that has placed him at the centre of both snubs. Shafali Verma's 64 guides India into Women's Asia Cup final The stand-off unfolded against a backdrop of long-running tensions between nuclear-armed neighbours India and Pakistan. A year on from beating Pakistan in the final, the men's side have still not collected their trophy. Sunday's ceremony was delayed by nearly 50 minutes before it descended further, with Naqvi distributing medals only to the runners-up before the event ended abruptly. India's players were left to present medals to themselves, with BCCI secretary Devajit Saikia and vice-president Rajeev Shukla looking on from the ground. Spinners star as India crush Pakistan by 7 wickets in Women's Asia Cup T20 "That stand has been taken by BCCI (Indian cricket board), and we stand by it," Indian women's coach Amol Muzumdar told reporters, defending the decision to snub the presentation. "We are the champions, that's good enough."

gb.title: Sapiens Announces Its AI-Native Autonomous Insurance Platform (SapiensAIP)
gb.description: Sapiens International Corporation N.V. today announced the launch of its AI - native Sapiens Autonomous Insurance Platform (SapiensAIP) – a modern, SaaS solution that helps insurers move from AI ambition to production with built in tools to embed AI in their core policy administration system (PAS). SapiensAIP is a unified platform, built to extend Sapiens’ core insurance products and unlocks a full suite of agentic tools across underwriting, policy, billing, claims, and customer engagement. The platform is built on three layers: a persona-based experience layer, an intelligence layer where agentic flows do the work, and a foundation layer, based on Sapiens’ ontology of more than 40 years of industry experience. This foundation gives every AI agent the context to reason like an insurer. It also grounds Sapiens’ dedicated data migration and configuration hubs. These hubs take requirements and legacy files and turn them into run-ready scripts and load-ready extracts that are mapped, proven and reversible, taking human effort out while retaining human oversight of any transformation. “The AI future we have been talking about is here,” said Sapiens Executive Chairman and interim CEO Mike Ettling. “The architecture behind SapiensAIP is the clearest expression yet of what Sapiens has become: the global insurance technology champion built to power the modern autonomous insurer of tomorrow, with a continuously improving layer of intelligence. This is an advantage no legacy architecture retrofitted with AI can match.” First SapiensAIP customer Sapiens also announced Continental General (CG), an Austin, Texas-based Third-Party Administrator (TPA) serving multiple clients across life, annuity, and long-term care and stock life, accident and health insurance carrier is evaluating the AI tools as a means to be able to bring on books of business faster and more cost-effectively. "SapiensAIP represents the kind of platform direction we want from our technology partners – AI that’s embedded in the core system, not bolted on. As a third-party administrator serving multiple carrier clients, Continental General needs tooling that can scale across programs and compress the timeline from contract to production. We’re putting the Configuration Hub and Migration Hub to work against real workflows, and the early direction is promising," said Ayanna Burns, Chief Transformation Officer, Continental General. Speeding up transformation With legacy core transformation an ongoing challenge for insurers, SapiensAIP Migration Hub now speeds up lengthy transformations, mergers or acquisitions by safely handling four steps with agent swarms: profiling, mapping, validating, and extracting data. Legacy files are ingested exactly as they are, with no reformatting needed. The Migration Hub AI suggests how old data should map to the new system, providing a confidence score that customer subject matter experts review. With SapiensAIP Configuration Hub, configuration stops being the project bottleneck and is now handled by AI in the background. It takes documents in any format and automatically maps them to the right field in any system. Its confidence mapping score means that teams can review and approve what moves forward. Every decision has an auditable trail. “SapiensAIP is what turns AI ambition into results insurers can measure,” said Sapiens CEO Designate and Board member, Paul Wheeler. “The work we are doing with Continental General shows exactly this. For insurers, this means faster time to production, lower transformation risk and a return on investment in AI working in their core systems, right now.” NoYes Artificial Intelligence 14 Sep, 2026

mx.title: Vecinos de Miacatlán piden nebulización y abate
mx.description: Ante proliferación de mosquitos, llaman a autoridades a aplicar medidas para prevenir casos de dengue. Miacatlán.- Habitantes de la cabecera municipal hicieron un llamado a las autoridades de Salud para reforzar las acciones de prevención y control del mosquito, ante el incremento en su presencia en distintas zonas de la localidad. Los vecinos solicitaron que se lleven a cabo jornadas de nebulización y se fortalezca la distribución de abate para el tratamiento de depósitos de agua, particularmente en aquellos sitios donde las condiciones favorecen la reproducción del mosquito. Señalaron que después de las lluvias registradas en las últimas semanas, se han generado acumulaciones de agua en patios, recipientes, lotes y otros espacios, situación que puede convertirse en criaderos del mosquito Aedes aegypti, transmisor del dengue, zika y chikungunya. Ante esta situación, los habitantes consideraron necesario que las autoridades municipales y sanitarias intensifiquen las labores de control larvario, nebulización y descacharrización, además de mantener campañas de información para que las familias eliminen de sus viviendas cualquier recipiente que pueda acumular agua. Los pobladores señalaron que la participación ciudadana es fundamental, pero consideraron que debe complementarse con acciones institucionales, principalmente en las zonas donde se ha detectado una mayor presencia de mosquitos. Finalmente hicieron un llamado a las autoridades de Salud para atender la petición y establecer un programa de intervención en la cabecera municipal, con el propósito de reducir la presencia del vector y prevenir posibles casos de enfermedades transmitidas por mosquito. #miacatlan #Dengue

mx.title: Nuevo fallo detectado: si tienes un ordenador Windows, revisa esto antes de que te pase
mx.description: Microsoft actualizó este mismo mes de septiembre Windows 11, y es precisamente esta última versión la que está provocando un error muy concreto en algunos ordenadores. El fallo tiene que ver con que determinados dispositivos de audio conectados por USB pueden dejar de funcionar correctamente. La propia Microsoft ya ha reconocido el fallo, tal y como también reporta Bleeping Computer , y ha incluido la incidencia entre los problemas conocidos de sus últimas actualizaciones, por lo que conviene comprobar qué versión de Windows tienes instalada si el sonido ha empezado a comportarse de forma extraña. Ahora bien, el problema no afecta a todos los usuarios ni a cualquier dispositivo de sonido. Está relacionado con determinados equipos que utilizan dispositivos USB Audio Class 1.0 y, según Microsoft, puede aparecer después de instalar las actualizaciones de seguridad lanzadas el 8 de septiembre de 2026. Problema de sonido en Windows 11 Las actualizaciones afectadas son KB5124008 , de Windows 11 24H2 y 25H2, y KB5124012 , correspondiente a Windows 11 26H1. Ambas forman parte del paquete de actualizaciones de septiembre de Microsoft. La compañía ha reconocido que algunos dispositivos USB Audio Class 1.0 pueden no iniciarse correctamente después de instalar estas actualizaciones. En los casos afectados, Windows puede mostrar el mensaje “Este dispositivo no puede iniciarse (Código 10)” en el Administrador de dispositivos. El fallo puede manifestarse de varias maneras. El ordenador puede detectar que existe un dispositivo de audio conectado, pero no reproducir ningún sonido. También pueden dejar de responder correctamente algunos controles relacionados con el volumen o la configuración de sonido del sistema. La incidencia es especialmente relevante para quienes utilizan DAC USB, altavoces , interfaces de audio o determinados dispositivos externos en lugar de la salida de sonido integrada del ordenador. No significa, por tanto, que todos los PC con Windows 11 estén afectados. Microsoft corrige su software muy a menudo. Montaje de ADSLZone Audio multicanal Algunos usuarios también han informado de problemas cuando utilizan configuraciones de audio multicanal. Entre ellas aparecen funciones como el audio 3D o los modos de ocho canales. Una de las soluciones, al menos temporales, podría ser cambiar el dispositivo a una configuración de dos canales . No obstante, Microsoft todavía no ha publicado una solución oficial definitiva para esta incidencia, por lo que no debería considerarse como el método correcto para arreglarlo.

Con los jugadores es lo mismo, más o menos cansados pero hay que ir a por ellos -los rivales-. Al Elche y el Atlético de Madrid les pasa lo mismo que a nosotros. Si me decís que la próxima semana de seis ahorramos una rueda de prensa traigo aquí algo de picar y nos divertimos”, bromeó en la rueda de prensa de este lunes, previa al duelo contra el Elche (martes, 21.30 horas).

ph.title: Smart Home WiFi SIM 99 Lets Users Reconnect Compatible Routers for PHP 99
ph.description: Smart Home WiFi SIM 99 gives users an affordable way to bring compatible existing Home WiFi routers back online, complete with 2GB of non-expiring data and access to Smart Home WiFi data promos. Affordable Access: Priced at just PHP 99 , the Smart Home WiFi SIM 99 comes with 2GB of non-expiring data, offering households, dormers, boarders, and small businesses an affordable starting point for home internet connectivity using compatible existing routers. Router Revival: The dedicated Home WiFi SIM works with open-line Home WiFi routers as well as compatible Smart and PLDT Home WiFi devices with expired or inactive SIMs, allowing customers to put existing hardware back to use instead of immediately purchasing a new router. Flexible Connectivity: Beyond its included data, users can register for Smart Home WiFi BIG DATA and UNLI promos according to their connectivity needs, while the SIM is also 5G-ready for access to the Smart 5G network when paired with compatible equipment. Have an open-line Home WiFi router sitting around at home, or perhaps a Smart or PLDT Home WiFi device that has stopped being useful because its SIM has expired or become inactive? Smart Communications, Inc. (Smart) is giving these devices another chance to get connected with the new Smart Home WiFi SIM 99 . Available for only PHP 99 , the dedicated SIM is designed exclusively for Home WiFi routers and already comes with 2GB of non-expiring data. It provides an affordable entry point for households that need reliable connectivity without necessarily having to invest in new Home WiFi hardware. Make the Most of Existing Routers One of the biggest practical advantages of the Smart Home WiFi SIM 99 is its compatibility with open-line Home WiFi routers. It can also be used with compatible Smart and PLDT Home WiFi devices equipped with expired or inactive SIMs. For users who already have one of these routers at home, this means they may be able to put their existing device back to work rather than buying new hardware. That can make a meaningful difference for customers who simply need a practical and flexible way to connect multiple devices to the internet. Prepaid Home WiFi routers have become a particularly useful connectivity option in places where fiber internet is not yet available. They can serve families connecting multiple gadgets at home, dormers and boarders who require internet access in temporary living spaces, and small businesses that rely on connectivity for their everyday operations. Lloyd R. Manaloto , First Vice President and OIC for Smart, said, “With the Smart Home WiFi SIM 99, we are giving customers a convenient and affordable way to make the most of their existing Home WiFi devices and enjoy Smart’s connectivity for seamless online activities, whether they are working, studying, streaming, gaming, or simply staying connected with loved ones.” More Data Options When Needed The included 2GB of non-expiring data gives users an immediate allocation to get started. Since the data does not expire, customers can use it according to their own needs instead of having to consume the allocation within a limited validity period. For households and users who require more data, Smart Home WiFi SIM 99 subscribers can also register for Smart Home WiFi's BIG DATA and UNLI promos. This gives customers the flexibility to select data options depending on how they intend to use their connection. Users can register their new SIM through the official Smart SIM Registration portal. Once connected, they can also conveniently manage their Home WiFi data offers through the Smart App, making it easier to choose and register for available promos. Powered by Smart 5G Smart Home WiFi SIM 99 is also 5G-ready, giving customers access to the Smart 5G network when used with compatible devices and where the service is available. For users, this connectivity can support everyday online activities ranging from video streaming and gaming to real-time file sharing and social media updates. This makes the SIM relevant not just for casual internet use but also for households and small businesses whose daily routines increasingly depend on being connected. Smart was also recently recognized by Ookla® for delivering the Best Mobile Video Experience in the Philippines for the first half of 2026. According to the recognition cited by Smart, the network recorded a Video Score of 72.82, the highest among mobile operators in the country during the period. Price and Availability The Smart Home WiFi SIM 99 is priced at PHP 99 and includes 2GB of non-expiring data. It is now available through Smart Stores, authorized retail outlets, and distributors nationwide. Customers who prefer to purchase online can also get the SIM through the Smart Online Store. For people who already own a compatible Home WiFi router that is no longer being used, Smart Home WiFi SIM 99 presents a straightforward way to give that hardware another purpose. Rather than letting an open-line router or a compatible Smart or PLDT Home WiFi device with an inactive SIM gather dust, users now have an affordable option for getting it connected again. At PHP 99 , with non-expiring starter data, access to additional BIG DATA and UNLI promos, and 5G readiness, the new SIM provides another flexible prepaid connectivity choice for Filipino households, renters, and small businesses looking to make better use of the Home WiFi hardware they already have. ph.title: Arellano torches San Sebastian for winning start in NCAA
ph.description: MANILA, Philippines — ARELLANO used a blistering first quarter to drub San Sebastian, 98-72, in Group B of the NCAA Season 102 men’s basketball tournament at the San Juan Arena on Monday. The Chiefs opened the game with a feisty 10-0 run and never looked back, taking a 34-22 lead after the opening quarter. “We prepared physically and mentally. They may not see everything we’ve been doing behind the scenes, but aside from that, the players made a commitment to this season,” coach Chico Manabat said. “They played until the end. We saw the killer instinct that we’ve been talking about.” Things only got worse for the Golden Stags in the second period as Arellano blew the game wide open, taking an insurmountable 61-36 lead at halftime. The Chiefs continued to pull away in the second half, leading by as many as 29 points at 84-55. T-Mc Ongotan led the charge for the Chiefs with 23 points, six assists and three steals, while Basty Valencia and Renzo Abiera chipped in 12 points apiece in the victory. Matt Acosta’s double-double of 13 points and 11 rebounds went to waste for the Stags, while John Ynot also scored 13 points in the defeat.

Each one arrives in a fresh gradient colorway and a clear capsule that shows exactly how much juice is left, bringing the PUREX 60K family to 17 flavors in the U.S. DOJO PUREX 60K Introduces Blast Edition: Five New Flavors for the World’s First INSTA-JUICEDTM Vape The Blast Edition vibe: fruit first, sweetness kept just right, and a cool finish that keeps it easy from morning to late night. The Mega Clear Capsule keeps the e-liquid level in plain sight, with no guessing about what's left, and an ultra leak-proof design keeps pockets and bags clean. ae.title: Dubai Metro network to grow 80% as Gold Line tender nears
ae.description: Dubai: Dubai's Roads and Transport Authority (RTA) is currently implementing the Dubai Metro Blue Line project and plans to launch the tender for the Gold Line project by the end of this year, according to Mattar Al Tayer, Director-General and Chairman of the Board of Executive Directors of the RTA. Al Tayer said the combined cost of the two projects is estimated at around Dh55 billion. The projects will increase the length of the Dubai Metro network from 90km currently to 162km after the completion of the Blue Line in 2029 and the Gold Line in 2032, representing an 80% increase. He said Dubai's metro projects are being delivered according to the highest international standards, following clear plans and precise timelines, under the supervision of national and international engineers and experts whose combined experience exceeds 2,500 years. Al Tayer was speaking during a press conference announcing the first edition of the Dubai International Rail Conference and Exhibition 2027, which will be held at the Dubai World Trade Centre from May 31 to June 2, 2027. Held under the theme "Building the Future of Railways and Mobility", the event is expected to attract more than 5,000 participants and over 60 exhibitors from international companies and institutions. More than 70 speakers, including officials, decision-makers, industry leaders and specialists, will take part in discussions on developments in the railway sector and the future of sustainable mobility. Al Tayer said railway networks and modern transport systems are key drivers of economic growth, urban development and sustainability, while also improving quality of life and strengthening connectivity between communities and markets. He noted that railways form the backbone of mass transit systems, adding that the Dubai Metro accounts for 40% of total public transport users in the emirate and has carried nearly three billion passengers since its launch on September 9, 2009. For his part, Abdulmohsen Ibrahim, Executive Director of the Rail Agency at the RTA, said the Blue Line project is progressing on schedule and has not been directly affected by recent geopolitical developments in the region. He said the project is set to open on September 9, 2029, and has reached 24% completion.

sa.title: برشلونة مرشح لمواصلة بدايته المثالية في الدوري الإسباني
sa.description:
بدو برشلونة مرشحا لمواصلة بدايته المثالية في حملة الدفاع عن لقبه، حين يستضيف راسينغ سانتاندر في أول مواجهة بين الفريقين في الدوري الإسباني لكرة القدم منذ آذار/مارس 2012.
وخرج فريق المدرب الألماني هانزي فليك منتصرا من المراحل الخمس الأولى من الدوري، آخرها الأحد على حساب مضيفه ليفانتي 4-2 بفضل ثنائية لنجمه الشاب لامين جمال، ليكون وحيدا في الصدارة بفارق ثلاث نقاط عن وصيفه وغريمه ريال مدريد الذي يلتقي الثلاثاء مع مضيفه إلتشي.
وسجل الفريق الكاتالوني، الفائز أيضا في منتصف الأسبوع الماضي على فينورد الهولندي 5-1 في مستهل مشواره في دوري أبطال أوروبا، 21 هدفا في خمس مباريات في "لا ليغا"، أي بمعدل أكثر من أربعة أهداف في المباراة الواحدة.
ورغم أن سانتاندر حقق بداية موفقة في مستهل عودة إلى دوري الكبار للمرة الأولى منذ 2012 بجمعه 7 نقاط من خمس مباريات، سيكون من الصعب جدا عليه أن يفاجئ مضيفه الكاتالوني الذي لم يخسر أمام منافسه منذ كانون الثاني/يناير 2004 (0-3).
والتقى الفريقان الموسم الماضي في ثمن نهائي مسابقة الكأس وحقق برشلونة فوزه الثامن تواليا على منافسه (2-0) والخامس عشر في آخر 18 مواجهة، في سلسلة من دون هزيمة.
قد يكون برشلونة حقق العلامة الكاملة حتى الآن بفوزه في مبارياته الخمس، لكن هشاشته الدفاعية انكشفت الأحد بعدما قلص ليفانتي الفارق من 0-3 إلى 2-3 في الدقائق الأخيرة.
وحسم البديل الألماني كريم أدييمي المباراة لبرشلونة في الوقت بدلا من الضائع بهدف فردي رائع.
- "لم تكن أفضل مباراة لنا" -
وقال فليك للصحافيين "لم تكن أفضل مباراة لنا بالطبع. بدأنا بشكل رائع، لكننا عانينا قليلا في الشوط الثاني. علينا أن نواصل العمل من أجل التحسن. هذا أمر طبيعي، فهناك أمور يجب أن ننفذها بصورة أفضل، بل أفضل بكثير. سنوضح ذلك للفريق ثم نركز على المباراة المقبلة، لكني سعيد بالنتيجة".
من جانبه، قال مدافع برشلونة إريك غارسيا لشبكة "موفيستار" إن الفريق استرخى بعض الشيء في الشوط الثاني وكاد يدفع ثمن ذلك، مضيفا "كانت مباراة صعبة، وقد جعلناها أكثر تعقيدا مما كان ينبغي".
واستطرد "لكن يجب أن نتعلم من ذلك. إذا منحت أي منافس مساحة لالتقاط أنفاسه، فسيفرض سيطرته عليك."
ومن جهته، يحل ريال مدريد ضيفا الثلاثاء على إلتشي الذي جمع نقطتين فقط من مبارياته الخمس الأولى، مع هدف العودة بالنقاط الثلاث والبقاء قريبا من غريمه الكاتالوني.
وعاد فريق المدرب البرتغالي جوزيه مورينيو إلى الانتصارات، بعد السقوط على أرض ريال بيتيس 0-1، بفوزه على إنتر الإيطالي 1-0 في دوري أبطال أوروبا ثم التغلب على رايو فايكانو 4-1 في المرحلة الماضية بثنائية من الفرنسي كيليان مبابي.
ورأى مورينيو، العائد لتجربة تدريبية ثانية مع النادي الملكي بعد خروج الأخير من الموسم الماضي من دون ألقاب، أن "الفوز كان مهما جدا، خصوصا بعد خسارتنا المباراة الأخيرة في الدوري الإسباني".
وتابع "حسمنا المباراة في الشوط الأول (بالتقدم 3-0)، وهذا ليس بالأمر السهل، بعد العمل الذي بذلناه عقب مباراة دوري أبطال أوروبا، ليس بدنيا فقط، بل ذهنيا أيضا".
وعلى غرار برشلونة، يواجه ريال فريقا غابت عنه الانتصارات على النادي الملكي منذ فترة طويلة جدا، وتحديدا منذ آذار/مارس 1978 حين فاز عليه 3-1 في الدوري، قبل أن يفشل بعدها في تحقيق الفوز لـ19 مباراة متتالية بين الدوري والكأس.
لكن على ريال ألا يكرر سيناريو زيارته الأخيرة إلى ملعب منافسه حين اكتفى بالتعادل 2-2 الموسم الماضي، بعدما كان في طريقه للسقوط قبل أن ينقذه الإنكليزي جود بيلينغهام بهدف في الرمق الأخير.
ويأمل ألافيس مواصلة بدايته الرائعة التي شهدت جمعه 10 نقاط من المباريات الخمس الأولى ليحتل المركز الثالث بفارق الأهداف أمام أتلتيكو مدريد وإشبيلية، حين يستضيف فالنسيا الجريح الذي اكتفى بنقطة حتى الآن، ما دفعه الأحد إلى فسخ عقد مدربه كارلوس كوربيران، الموجود في منصبه منذ كانون الأول/ديسمبر 2024، ومديره التنفيذي البريطاني رون غورلاي.
وسيتولى أوسكار سانشيس، مدرب الفريق الرديف، المهمة بشكل موقت إلى حين تعيين مدرب جديد.

za.title: SAFA to pursue legal costs from Ledwaba, Mohlabeng
za.description:
SAFA to pursue legal costs from Ledwaba, Mohlabeng Nokuthula Khanyile Mon, 09/14/2026 - 12:10

JOHANNESBURG - The South African Football Association (SAFA) is preparing to pursue former presidential challengers Ria Ledwaba and Solly Mohlabeng for legal costs incurred during a series of court battles against the association.

Under re-elected president Danny Jordaan, SAFA says it will take legal steps to recover money spent defending multiple challenges brought by the duo.

The association is expected to send its first claim to Ledwaba and Mohlabeng in the coming days.

The move follows the recent dismissal, with costs, of their Constitutional Court application for leave to appeal.

READ | Danny Jordaan re-elected as SAFA president

Ledwaba and Mohlabeng had sought to overturn the outcome of SAFA’s 2022 presidential election. They also challenged their loss of standing within the association’s structures.

Their latest legal setback resulted in a costs order against them, which SAFA now intends to pursue.

The development comes shortly after Jordaan secured another term as the head of South African football’s governing body.

Jordaan was re-elected for a fourth term at SAFA’s elective congress this past weekend, defeating challenger Sandile Zungu.

He received 157 votes, while Zungu secured 82.

India hammered Sri Lanka by 72 runs in the T20 final in Dubai on Sunday but Harmanpreet Kaur's side skipped the trophy presentation, repeating the stance of the men's team last year.

On both occasions, the trophy was supposed to have been handed over by Naqvi in his role as head of the Asian Cricket Council.

Naqvi is also Pakistan's interior minister and head of the country's cricket board.

There are long-running tensions between nuclear-armed neighbours India and Pakistan.

A year after beating Pakistan in the final, the men's side have still not collected their trophy.

"That stand has been taken by BCCI (Indian cricket board), and we stand by it," Indian women's coach Amol Muzumdar told reporters.

"We are the champions, that's good enough."

Sunday's presentation was delayed by nearly 50 minutes, after which Naqvi distributed medals to the runners-up before the ceremony ended abruptly.

BCCI secretary Devajit Saikia and vice-president Rajeev Shukla were at the ground as India presented medals to their players themselves.

za.title: Is it possible to slow down the development of AI?
za.description:
Is it possible to slow down the development of AI? Estelle.Bronkhorst Mon, 09/14/2026 - 12:00

WASHINGTON - Top AI executives say they want to slow the breakneck pace of artificial intelligence development, but competition, US government reluctance and geopolitical factors stand in the way.

- What are AI leaders proposing? -

On Saturday, Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei advocated for a coordinated slowdown of AI development to better understand the risks arising from the technology's capabilities.

He received public support from his counterpart at OpenAI, Sam Altman, as well as from Elon Musk and Google DeepMind chief Demis Hassabis.

- Why now? -

In recent months, OpenAI and Anthropic have reported several incidents in which AI systems spontaneously broke out of their confined environments to access the internet and attack websites and platforms.

These AI systems demonstrated the ability to coordinate, establish hierarchies among themselves, cheat and erase traces of their actions.

Meanwhile, on Tuesday, Jacob Coxon -- who resigned from Anthropic and previously worked at OpenAI -- publicly accused both startups of lax security standards and "gambling with our lives."

- Will they slow down on their own? -

Competition among the industry's leading players is so fierce, with hundreds of billions of dollars in investment at stake, that none of them is willing to risk easing off the accelerator alone.

Amodei has expressed a willingness to coordinate with rivals, excluding China.

When asked by AFP about potential discussions to this end, Anthropic, OpenAI and Google did not immediately respond.

For now, the only concrete measure adopted by both Anthropic and OpenAI is the inclusion of independent observers who will internally verify the companies' work regarding AI safety.

- Is this a PR stunt? -

While many in the industry welcomed Amodei's message, others questioned his motives.

For Brian Roemmele, an entrepreneur and figure in the AI sector, it amounts to a sales pitch delivered just weeks before Anthropic is likely to take shares public.

"That is the IPO story in essay form: we are the responsible firm; we are the cure; buy the safety premium," he posted on X, referring to widely expected initial public offering.

Several figures in tech private equity also accused Anthropic of "regulatory capture" -- seeking to have public authorities cement, through regulation, a hierarchy with the startup at the top.

"Stop pretending the motivation to slow down is purely altruistic," said David Sacks, a former AI advisor to President Donald Trump who remains influential at the White House.

"You face massive product-liability exposure if your products enable a truly damaging cyberattack," he said.

- Can AI slow down without the Trump administration's support? -

On Sunday, Trump dismissed the warnings from AI industry leaders as "negative forces."

Several Republicans have expressed reluctance to actively regulate the technology, fearing it could stifle innovation and risk letting China win the AI race, according to House Speaker Mike Johnson.

On Sunday, Amodei reiterated the need for government oversight of AI. Like Altman and Hassabis, he believes that rules set by the industry itself would be insufficient.

- Can the brakes be applied without China? -

Anthropic's Amodei suggests limiting coordination to democratic countries, excluding China.

However, the AI race and China's advances in the field create "the toughest dilemma" regarding whether or not to slow down AI development, he noted on CBS on Sunday.

The United States plans to discuss AI safety on the sidelines of Chinese leader Xi Jinping's late September visit to Washington. But China is wary of any US attempt to impose its own regulatory framework, according to several media outlets.

This divergence is particularly pronounced given that China encourages the emergence of so-called "open" AI-systems that are freely accessible and modifiable -- in contrast to the "closed" models favored by major US companies.

Open AI models are, by definition, harder to control, as users can alter their parameters -- potentially for malicious purposes.

To allow leading non-Chinese companies to ease off the accelerator, Amodei urges stricter export controls on the most advanced US chips to China and better safeguards against the misappropriation of Western AI technology by Chinese laboratories.

  • by Thomas Urbain (AFP)

zw.title: Stanbic Bank Zimbabwe launches awards to reward SMEs
zw.description: Business Reporter STANBIC Bank Zimbabwe has launched ‘The Standard Bank Africa Business Awards’ aimed at celebrating and recognising exceptional small and medium-sized enterprises (SMEs) across Africa. The Standard Bank Africa Business Awards are the first of their kind and seek to play a pivotal role in driving innovation, resilience, leadership and economic impact within industries and communities. Stanbic Bank head of business and commercial banking, Mr Patson Mahatchi, said the awards are open to eligible SMEs across Africa, including businesses that do not currently bank with Standard Bank Group or Stanbic Bank. Mr Mahatchi said the awards have been established to celebrate and recognise impactful businesses driving growth, innovation and excellence across the continent. The awards feature five categories designed to recognise excellence across key sectors and business segments, including: agriculture; construction; Fast Moving Consumer Goods and retail, manufacturing, women in business and youth-owned businesses. Mr Mahatchi said Stanbic Bank was honoured to celebrate the entrepreneurs, innovators, and business leaders who are shaping Zimbabwe’s economy and contributing to Africa’s growth story through the awards. He said Stanbic Bank is cognizant of the fact that small and medium-sized enterprises across Zimbabwe are creating jobs, developing innovative solutions, strengthening communities, and unlocking opportunities that drive sustainable economic growth. “At Stanbic Bank, we firmly believe that SMEs are the engine of economic development. Driven by our purpose; ‘Zimbabwe is Our Home, We Drive Her Growth’, we continue to support businesses with access to financial solutions, advisory services, market opportunities, and platforms that enable growth,” he said. Mr Mahatchi said The Africa Business Awards also seek to recognise and celebrate those businesses that demonstrate excellence, innovation, growth, and positive social impact. More importantly, these awards provide an opportunity for Zimbabwean businesses to gain continental recognition and showcase their achievements on a larger African stage. He said Stanbic Bank recognizes that extraordinary businesses already exist within Zimbabwe and that their stories deserve to be told. Their achievements deserve to be celebrated while their contribution to economic transformation deserve recognition. “We, therefore, encourage businesses from across Zimbabwe, regardless of size or sector, to participate in these awards,” said Mr Mahatchi, adding that participants can be drawn from those SMEs who would have pioneered innovation, expanded exports, empowered communities, embraced sustainability, or created employment among many others. He said Stanbic Bank Zimbabwe’s commitment extends beyond banking adding that the institution is committed to enabling growth, fostering entrepreneurship, and supporting the ambitions of businesses that will define Africa’s future. “These awards reflect that commitment. To all entrepreneurs and business owners, I encourage you to seize this opportunity, share your story, celebrate your achievements and inspire others. “Let Zimbabwe’s business excellence be represented among the very best on the continent,” said Mr Mahatchi. Stanbic Bank Zimbabwe head of enterprise banking, Sarah Charangwa said the awards are open to registered SMEs operating within eligible African markets where Standard Bank or Stanbic Bank has a presence. The group operates in 21 sub-Saharan African countries, including its anchor market of South Africa, plus countries such Angola, Kenya, Nigeria, and Zimbabwe. She said SMEs may enter multiple categories, provided that each submission is completed separately and meets the specific criteria for the relevant category. Businesses may enter the category that best aligns with their core business activities and demonstrated impact. Charangwa said entries will be assessed against criteria including: leadership and vision; innovation and creativity; sustainability and resilience; market and community impact; business growth and scalability as well as financial performance. “Entries will be reviewed by an independent panel comprising business leaders, industry experts, entrepreneurs and representatives from Standard Bank Group and partner organisations. Charangwa said winners stand to receive recognition, networking opportunities, funding, business exposure, mentorship opportunities and other benefits associated with the awards. “Startups may apply provided they are formally registered and able to demonstrate measurable business activity, innovation and growth potential,” she said.

mg.title: PROJET ÉNERGÉTIQUE - Le barrage de Volobe remis sur les rails
mg.description: De retour de sa tournée européenne, le colonel Randrianirina a annoncé la relance du projet de centrale hydroélectrique de Volobe. L’État compte entrer au capital de ce chantier d’envergure, tandis que la question du prix du kilowattheure serait désormais réglée. Le chef de l’État et les membres de l’Exécutif face à la presse, vendredi, à Ivato. Nous allons relancer le projet Volobe. » C’est l’une des principales annonces faites à la presse par le chef de l’État, le colonel Michaël Randrianirina, à son retour d’Europe dans la nuit de vendredi. Selon ses explications, la construction de ce barrage et de sa centrale hydroélectrique a occupé une place centrale dans ses échanges à l’étranger. Lors de son entretien avec Emmanuel Macron au palais de l’Élysée, le président français « s’est engagé à appuyer le plaidoyer de Madagascar auprès de l’Union européenne (UE)» afin d’obtenir un financement via le Fonds vert pour le climat. De même, le Premier ministre belge, Bart De Wever, a assuré le soutien de la Belgique sur ce dossier. Le locataire d’Iavoloha a précisé que l’exécutif entend mobiliser les subventions de ce mécanisme onusien créé en 2010 pour aider les pays en développement à favoriser une économie à faibles émissions de carbone, afin de financer sa prise de participation. Le colonel Randrianirina a par ailleurs affirmé que la Banque mondiale avait également manifesté sa volonté de soutenir financièrement l’entrée de l’État dans le capital de l’infrastructure. Les débuts du projet, plus précisément baptisé Volobe II, remontent à 2016. Les premières conventions avaient alors été signées entre l’État et la Compagnie générale d’hydroélectricité de Volobe (CGHV). L’ambition est de bâtir, sur la rivière Ivondro (région Atsinanana), un site d’une capacité estimée à 120 mégawatts (MW). Cependant, en raison de négociations enlisées et du retrait de certains membres du consortium, le chantier peine à décoller depuis dix ans. Le tarif de l’électricité a longtemps constitué le principal point d’achoppement des tractations. La CGHV réclamait 17 cents de dollar par kilowattheure, tandis que l’État tablait sur 9 cents. Si la durée de la concession a été fixée à vingt-cinq ans par la signature d’un contrat en 2023, le bouclage financier reste en suspens. Des points de blocage enfin levés Lors de son passage à Madagascar en avril 2025, Emmanuel Macron avait annoncé l’intégration d’Électricité de France (EDF) au consortium, mais cette entrée n’a pas permis de boucler le financement. En juillet dernier, le pouvoir de la Refondation a donc signé un avenant avec la CGHV pour prolonger les négociations jusqu’en juin 2027, maintenant les discussions sont ouvertes sur les coûts et l’actionnariat public. À s’en tenir aux déclarations présidentielles de vendredi, un compromis semble enfin trouvé pour mobiliser les fonds nécessaires. Bien que le chef de l’État n’ait pas précisé le montant de l’enveloppe que Madagascar s’apprête à injecter, cet investissement public aurait permis d’obtenir une baisse du tarif initialement proposé par l’opérateur. « La participation de l’État permettra d’avancer dans la réalisation de Volobe, tout en réduisant le coût de l’énergie pour les usagers », a assuré le colonel Randrianirina. Avec ses 120 MW annoncés, la future centrale devrait alimenter les Réseaux interconnectés d’Antananarivo (RIA) et de Toamasina. Comme l’a souligné le chef de l’État, « en matière énergétique, nous n’avions fait que colmater les brèches jusqu’ici». Volobe est ainsi présenté comme la solution durable à la crise énergétique nationale. Reste désormais à transformer ces promesses en réalité, alors que la relance de ce projet a déjà été annoncée à maintes reprises depuis dix ans. Garry Fabrice Ranaivoson

mg.title: FOOTBALL - INTERCLUBS CAF - CFFA passe, FC Rouge craque
mg.description: L’équipe d’Andoharanofotsy file au deuxième tour préliminaire de la Ligue des champions africaine. Le FC Rouge plie bagages pour sa part après une double défaite. Le club d’Andoharanofotsy savoure sa première qualification au second tour. Bel exploit. Le Centre de formation de football d’Andoharanofotsy (CFFA) s’est qualifié pour le deuxième tour de la Ligue des champions africaine. La formation malgache a éliminé les Lesothans du Lijabatho FC sur un score cumulé de 3 buts à 1. Après leur victoire (2-0) au match aller à Côte d’Or (Maurice) le 5 septembre, les joueurs d’Andoharanofotsy ont décroché un nul (1-1) au retour, samedi, au stade de Dobsonville en Afrique du Sud. Le score était encore vierge à la pause. L’attaquant vedette, Tendry Mataniah Raharijaona, a finalement ouvert la marque au retour des vestiaires (53e), avant que l’équipe adverse n’égalise en toute fin de rencontre (85e). « Ce match retour a été particulièrement rude, mais les joueurs se sont donnés à fond. Nous sommes très heureux de cette qualification pour le second tour, d’autant que notre dernière performance à ce niveau remonte à plusieurs années », se réjouit le coach Franck Rajaonarisamba. « Nous étions prêts et forts mentalement », a ajouté le technicien. Pour rappel, le Fosa Juniors FC était le dernier représentant malgache à avoir franchi le premier tour, en 2019. Fin de parcours pour le FC Rouge Le CFFA affrontera les Young Africans au prochain tour de la compétition. Les Tanzaniens ont écarté le club botswanais du Gaborone United sur un score cumulé de 2-1. En revanche, l’aventure s’achève prématurément en Coupe de la Confédération pour le vainqueur de la Coupe de Madagascar, le FC Rouge. Le club d’Alarobia Amboniloha s’est incliné à deux reprises (0-2) face aux Red Arrows zambiens : d’abord à l’aller le 5 septembre au stade Levy Mwanawasa à Ndola, puis au retour hier, au complexe sportif de Côte d’Or à Maurice. Les Zambiens ont dominé les débats hier, menant déjà un à zéro à la pause avant d’enfoncer le clou au retour des vestiaires (55e). «Ils sont nettement supérieurs en termes de gabarit et affichent une cohésion impressionnante sur le terrain. Les Red Arrows forment un grand club et ils l’ont prouvé. De notre côté, nous manquons cruellement de matchs de haut niveau », a reconnu le coach des Rouges, Fenosoa Ratolojanahary. Le FC Rouge plie ainsi bagages tandis que le CFFA poursuivra son épopée continentale, effaçant ainsi sa tentative ratée de 2023. Serge Rasanda

mg.title: RUN – CHAMPIONNAT DE MADAGASCAR - Nouroudine arrache une deuxième victoire
mg.description: Le champion national en titre et vainqueur de la précédente manche, Nouroudine Mamodaly, au volant d’une Audi TT, a confirmé sa suprématie hier à la base 213 d’Arivonimamo. Nouroudine Mamodaly, au volant de son Audi TT, remporte sa deuxième victoire consécutive. Belle bagarre. Le pilote du club RunMada, Nouroudine Mamodaly, au volant d’une Audi TT, s’est une nouvelle fois imposé hier lors de la course « 261 Back to Speed », comptant pour la troisième manche du championnat de Madagascar de run sur 400 m, disputée à la base 213 d’Arivonimamo. Le champion de Madagascar en titre, déjà vainqueur de la précédente manche « The King of Mada Fosa Energy » en juillet, a dominé en super finale Tahiana Rasolojaona, alias Jay Taxx, au volant d’une BMW E30. Nouroudine a réalisé un chrono de 9’’405 contre 9’’822 pour son adversaire. En demi-finale, il s’est imposé face au pilote de l’AMA Mano Ramaherniarivo, sur Peugeot 205 AMG, après avoir écarté Bryan Ratsivahiny, sur Peugeot 205 Tonnerre, en quarts de finale. Nouroudine a réalisé un chrono de 9’’071 lors de son quatrième passage joker. Il avait effectué son premier passage en 9’’128. Il détient également le record national, établi à 9’’030 lors de la deuxième manche du championnat. De son côté, Jay Taxx a signé le meilleur chrono de sa carrière, en 9’’05. « Tout allait bien. Nous avons dû gérer, car nous ne voulions pas trop forcer. Nous voulions rester tranquilles et rassurés. Nous avons pu réaliser ces performances grâce à mes préparateurs Don Octane, Speed Makers Voltand Germany et Tina Razafindrabe », souligne Nouroudine, leader provisoire du championnat. Combat et spectacle Jean de Dieu Rafanomezantsoa, dit Vazah, au volant d’une Subaru, a remporté la catégorie Pro Run 1, devant Mano, Jay Taxx et Nouroudine. Heriniaina Tahiry, du club AMA, s’est imposé en Super Run après avoir dominé Toala Rakotoarimanga, sur Peugeot 205, en finale. Dans la catégorie Run, la victoire est revenue à Sitraka Joelharson, dit « Tale », de RunMada, au volant d’une Honda Civic. Steven Ramalalaelison, du club AMA, sur AX T16, s’est imposé dans la catégorie des jeunes. Après l’accident mortel survenu lors de la précédente manche, l’équipe technique de la Fédération du sport automobile de Madagascar et le club organisateur, Mada Sport Auto (MSA), ont renforcé les mesures de sécurité avant le coup d’envoi de la course. Un test de freinage a notamment été rendu obligatoire et aucun véhicule n’a été autorisé à stationner aux abords de la zone d’arrivée. Deux autres manches nationales figurent encore au calendrier du championnat de Madagascar de run cette saison. La quatrième et avant-dernière se déroulera à Toamasina le 1er novembre. Serge Rasanda
